about: Engine knobs, one row each, keyed by engine, and how `boltbeam tune MODEL --engine E` sets them on the machine it runs on (workflow/tune.py reads it; engines.<E>.adapter is the module that reads that engine's build, supplies its facts, runs its measured points and writes its command). kind: env (an environment variable), flag (a command-line flag), config (a key of a JSON config flag, a.b). requires: the build features the knob needs (the adapter's detect: llama.cpp the getenv names compiled into the build, vLLM the flags its installed arg parser adds and the Literal values of its config classes); a row whose feature is missing is not in that build. group: the engine's named extra the knob comes from (a local patch), for the words. applies: an expression over facts. derive: facts (a formula, instant), measured (a short real-text prefill sweep under --measure, over the row's axis knob; without it the facts value or the default stands, said so), default (left at the default, with the evidence why). bitwise false: the knob changes outputs (said beside it). Formulas use only the facts in workflow/tune.FACTS and the adapter's namespaced facts (ns.name), numbers, strings, + - * / //, comparisons, and/or/not, x if c else y, min, max, pow2_floor, gib_floor, gib_ceil, floor_to. measured_when/measured: a clause of measured numbers a row adds to its reason only when the expression is true over this run's facts (the setup it was measured in), so a general reason never quotes another setup's numbers. Adding a knob is adding a row; adding an engine is a row under engines, its knobs and an adapter module.

llama-pinned-copy-stream.what: streams host-RAM experts to the GPU on a copy stream during prefill (v1: an L3-sized pinned ring; v2: a pinned copy made at load)

llama-moe-prefill.what: a parallel MoE routing sort, an MMQ tile-width knob and pinned staging for the server's state reads

llama-server-ckpt-min-head.what: no batch break and no checkpoint at a chat user-message start within the first N prompt tokens

llama-server-ckpt-tail-only.what: an opt-in that keeps only the context checkpoint before a prompt's last few tokens (one restore point)

knobs.name: --cache-ram
knobs.controls: llama-server's prompt cache in host RAM (MiB): it holds earlier requests' state in RAM
knobs.formula: 0 if (2 if llama_cpp.pin_in_build else 1) * host_expert_bytes + llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes + llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_bytes > usable_ram_bytes else None
knobs.reason: off when the host experts (counted twice when the build can pin them: the mmap pages the server still reads and a full pinned copy), the tables' resident rows and the default {llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_gib:.0f} GiB prompt cache exceed the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM; the pin budget below gets that RAM
knobs.reason_default: kept: the host experts (and a full pinned copy, when the build can pin), the tables' resident rows and the {llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_gib:.0f} GiB prompt cache fit the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM, so the prompt cache competes with nothing this tool sets (boltbeam recommend says when to turn it off)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 4: the save costs ~80 ms per 10k prompt; the offload runs all used --cache-ram 0

knobs.name: -ub
knobs.controls: the chunk of prompt tokens one forward pass reads (llama-server --ubatch-size); -b is raised with it
knobs.reason: the chunk BoltBeam's prompt limit picks for this machine (the offload page's prompt setup): the smallest within the policy tie of the best
knobs.measured: host experts are uploaded once per chunk, so bigger chunks upload less: with experts in RAM, 4096 measured 15% faster than 2048 (10k, -ncmoe 12, pinned: 4,312 vs 3,745 tok/s wall)
knobs.reason_default: llama-server's default: no prefill limit was computed here ({llama_cpp.plan_ubatch_why})

sweep.stop: two points in a row slower than the best by more than the tie

knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 3 (all-VRAM 10k: 2048 best, 2.7k: 4096), the offload match (-ub 4096) and the attribution audit (-ncmoe 12 pinned, 10k: -ub 4096 4,312 vs -ub 2048 3,745 tok/s wall)

knobs.name: -b
knobs.controls: the logical batch (llama-server --batch-size); a chunk (-ub) is never larger than it
knobs.reason: raised to -ub when -ub is larger (the command does it); a prompt is read in chunks of at most -ub, so a -b above -ub adds no larger chunk
knobs.measured: with experts in RAM, -b 8192 at -ub 4096 on a 10k prompt measured no effect: 4,295 vs 4,312 tok/s (the server's head and near-end breaks still set the decode calls)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md attribution audit, arm GVf

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS
knobs.controls: the weight streamer on (1) or off (0)
knobs.reason: on: it only engages for prefill chunks at or above the streamer's minimum chunk (the next row) with experts in host RAM; decode takes the stock path
knobs.measured: with Flash-Next experts in host RAM, decode was unchanged with it on (24.6 vs 24.8 tok/s)
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: the streamer has nothing to copy
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS_MIN_TOKENS
knobs.controls: the chunk size (tokens) from which a host expert tensor is uploaded whole on the copy stream instead of the stock routed-only, synchronous copy
knobs.reason: left at the patch's 1024: it decides only chunks smaller than it, so it matters only with a small -ub
knobs.measured: with Flash-Next experts in host RAM, at -ub 4096 on a 10k prompt 256 and 1024 read the same (4,329 vs 4,312 tok/s wall; the chat head batch is shorter than either); at -ub 256 and 512 the streamed path read 1.8-1.9x the stock one
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: the streamer has nothing to copy
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md attribution audit (GVa vs GV4: no change at -ub 4096; verdict: drop); llama-knob-derive-20261111.md (-ncmoe 12, all pinned: streamed 1.8-1.9x faster at -ub 256 and 512)

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS_PIN_GIB
knobs.controls: GiB of host experts copied once at load into pinned memory, which the GPU then reads at the full link rate
knobs.formula: gib_ceil(host_expert_bytes) if 2 * host_expert_bytes + llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes + llama_cpp.prompt_cache_bytes <= usable_ram_bytes else max(0, gib_floor(usable_ram_bytes - host_expert_bytes - llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes - llama_cpp.prompt_cache_bytes))
knobs.reason: a pinned copy is a second copy: the server's short chunks still read every host expert from the mmap, so all {host_expert_gib:.2f} GiB stay in the page cache. Pinned + host experts + tables' resident rows ({llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_gib:.2f} GiB) + prompt cache ({llama_cpp.prompt_cache_gib:.0f} GiB) must fit the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM ({ram_available_gib:.1f} GiB available when this ran, less the {ram_margin_gib:.0f} GiB margin). The margin makes it conservative. Run it with no other model server holding RAM. What it pins is whole expert tensors in load order, not experts by use: a routing profile (boltbeam routing MODEL --engine E{llama_cpp.routing_note}) says which experts a pin should hold first, which this patch cannot do yet, so that is advice only, not a setting
knobs.measured_when: has(gpu_name, 'RTX 5090') and has(model_file, 'Flash-Next') and ram_total_bytes > 30 * GiB and ram_total_bytes < 33 * GiB and host_expert_bytes > 0
knobs.measured: on an RTX 5090 with 31 GB of RAM and Flash-Next, -ncmoe 12/18/24 pinned in full read best (1.58-1.91x stock); with every expert in RAM (-cmoe) the rule allows 1 GiB where 4 GiB read best (+5% over none) and 8 GiB collapsed
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing to pin
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md v2: -ncmoe 12/18/24 all pinned best (1.58-1.91x stock); -cmoe 4 GiB best, 8/12 GiB collapsed (18-42k major faults per request) on 31 GB; kept by the attribution audit's verdict

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_RING_MIB
knobs.controls: the pinned staging ring the unpinned host experts are memcpy'd through (MiB)
knobs.reason: a quarter of the {l3_mib:.0f} MiB L3 the copying core shares ({l3_source}), a power of two: the memcpy's writes stay in cache and the DMA reads them from there, so staging is not DRAM-bound twice. The quarter comes from one L3 size; on any other it is derived, not measured
knobs.measured_when: has(gpu_name, 'RTX 5090') and has(model_file, 'Flash-Next') and l3_bytes == 32 * MiB
knobs.measured: on a 32 MiB L3 the quarter (8 MiB as 1 MiB x 8) read 1,661 tok/s, against 1,563 at 2 MiB, 1,463-1,485 at 16 MiB and 612 at 512 MiB
knobs.reason_default: the patch's 8 MiB: the L3 size could not be read ({l3_source})
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing is staged
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md tuning on a 32 MiB L3: 8 MiB (1 x 8) 1,661 tok/s; 2 MiB 1,563; 16 MiB 1,463-1,485; 512 MiB 612

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_CHUNK_KIB
knobs.controls: one staging copy's size (KiB): the ring holds ring / chunk copies in flight
knobs.reason: the ring in eight chunks, so the CPU fills one while the DMA drains the others; the count of eight comes from one L3 size, and on any other it is derived, not measured
knobs.measured_when: has(gpu_name, 'RTX 5090') and has(model_file, 'Flash-Next') and l3_bytes == 32 * MiB
knobs.measured: on a 32 MiB L3, 1 MiB x 8 read 1,661 tok/s against 4 MiB x 4 at 1,463 and 512 KiB x 4 at 1,563
knobs.reason_default: the patch's 1024 KiB: the L3 size could not be read ({l3_source})
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing is staged
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md tuning: 1 MiB x 8 1,661 vs 4 MiB x 4 1,463, 512 KiB x 4 1,563

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_SLOTS
knobs.controls: device slots the streamer uploads ahead into (prefetch depth); each slot grows to the largest host expert tensor it has held
knobs.reason: derived, not measured: as many slots as hiding the copy needs, but no more than fit beside the loaded model. Copy: the largest host expert tensor ({llama_cpp.host_expert_tensor_max_mib:.0f} MiB) takes {t.copy_ms:.1f} ms at this machine's {h2d_pinned_gbs:.1f} GB/s pinned copy rate (host scan). Compute: {t.layer_ms:.1f} ms per layer per {llama_cpp.chunk_tokens}-token chunk ({llama_cpp.prompt_compute_source}), {t.tensor_ms:.2f} ms per host tensor. So {t.lag} slots keep each copy ahead of its layer. The copy falls behind compute across the {llama_cpp.host_expert_tensors} host tensors, so {t.boundary} of the next chunk's first ones would have to be on the card before it starts, but only {t.tail} can be copied while the card's own layers finish the chunk before: {t.depth} are useful. Fit: {gpu_free_gib:.1f} GiB free now, less the model's {llama_cpp.on_card_gib:.1f} GiB on the card, the KV cache and recurrent state ({llama_cpp.kv_cache_gib:.2f} GiB), an estimated {t.compute_buffer_gib:.2f} GiB compute buffer and the {t.server_gib:.1f} GiB llama-server holds besides (its CUDA context and pools, seen once on an RTX 5090), leaves {t.after_load_gib:.1f} GiB after load; less a {t.margin_gib:.0f} GiB margin that is room for {t.fit} slots. The count is the smaller of the two, at most the {llama_cpp.host_expert_tensors} host expert tensors (more slots have nothing to hold) and never below the patch's 4. Too many slots is worse than too few: a slot that does not fit fails, and the streamer keeps retrying it
knobs.reason_missing: the patch's 4: the slot count could not be worked out here ({llama_cpp.vram_why})

sweep.what: start llama-server with the patch's 4 slots, read the GPU memory free after load and after one prompt, size the slots from that, then run them and back off while the log shows failed slot allocations
sweep.formula: max(4, min(llama_cpp.host_expert_tensors, t.depth, value + floor(max(0, llama_cpp.free_after_warm_bytes - 512 * MiB) / llama_cpp.host_expert_tensor_max_bytes)))
sweep.run_failed_words: the server did not start or did not answer
sweep.says: measured: with the patch's {measure.probe} slots llama-server left {llama_cpp.free_after_warm_gib:.1f} GiB of GPU memory free after one {prompt_tokens}-token prompt ({llama_cpp.free_after_load_gib:.1f} GiB right after load); less a 0.5 GiB slack (derived, not measured) that is room for {measure.first} slots of {llama_cpp.host_expert_tensor_max_mib:.0f} MiB (the copy needs {t.depth}, there are {llama_cpp.host_expert_tensors} host tensors). Run with them: {measure.runs}. {measure.value} ran with no failed slot allocation
sweep.says_none: measured: none of the counts tried ran without failed slot allocations ({measure.runs}); the derived value stands, and the log shows where it failed
sweep.stop: the first count that runs with no failed slot allocation, at most three runs

knobs.measured: on an RTX 5090 with 12 layers of Flash-Next experts in RAM (-ncmoe 12, 10k prompt), 4 slots read 5,415 tok/s wall, 8: 5,495, 12: 5,724, 16: 5,720, 24: 5,892 (n=6 at 4 and 24, n=2 between), with the copy left exposed at chunk starts down from 261.7 to 116.2 ms and outputs bitwise identical; 32 and 36 slots did not fit beside the loaded model (211 and 203 failed slot allocations) and ran slower, 5,062 and 5,231 (n=2). With 18 layers in RAM 36 slots fit and screened 5,722 vs 5,523 at 24 (n=2, not confirmed). Counts other than these are derived, not measured
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Step 2 (hide the copy at each ubatch start) and its add-on (slots-results.jsonl): the rule sizes from free memory after load because a count from an idle GPU (35) failed; the compute-buffer term is an estimate from the model's shapes (derived, not measured: this build's log does not print the buffer); t.server_bytes (1.7 GiB, 2026-11-11) is what a loaded llama-server held beyond this estimate on the RTX 5090 (tune-slots-measure: 6.90 GiB free after load where the estimate left 8.30, and 0.29 GiB more after one prompt beyond its 4 slots); replaces the earlier default-only row, whose 8 vs 4 result (llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md T2) was a different configuration

knobs.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_MIN_HEAD
knobs.controls: no batch break and no context checkpoint at a chat user-message start within the first N prompt tokens (0: stock, a break at every user start)
knobs.reason: 256 with experts in host RAM: the chat template's short head otherwise runs as its own batch, which uploads every host layer's experts from pageable memory and then takes a checkpoint sync. Outputs are not bitwise identical (the batch boundaries move); checkpoint restore still works

The first argmax divergences were near-ties (top-2 probabilities within 0.01-0.09), the same envelope as stock -ub 2048 vs 4096

knobs.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_TAIL_ONLY

knobs.formula: 1 if workload == 'one-shot' and host_expert_bytes > 0 else None

off, because the workload is chat (--workload chat, the default): with it on, a follow-up that changes an earlier part of the conversation re-reads the whole prompt; outputs of a single request are identical. Turn it on only for one-shot prompts (--workload one-shot)

knobs.name: --max-model-len
knobs.controls: the longest context vLLM serves; it must find KV cache room for one sequence this long at start
knobs.reason: the {context_tokens}-token context this setup is sized for (--context): the rows below fit the KV cache for it, and unset vLLM takes the model's whole context and must fit that
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/model.py:217 (default None: the model's own length); vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:999 (check_enough_kv_cache_memory); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:951

knobs.name: --gpu-memory-utilization
knobs.controls: the share of the GPU's total memory vLLM takes for weights, activations and the KV cache
knobs.formula: max(0.01, floor_to((gpu_free_bytes - GiB) / gpu_total_bytes, 0.01)) if (gpu_free_bytes - GiB) / gpu_total_bytes >= vllm.min_share and gpu_free_bytes - GiB < 0.92 * gpu_total_bytes else None
knobs.reason: the free share of the GPU now ({gpu_free_gib:.1f} of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB) less 1 GiB for vLLM's own CUDA context, which exists before vLLM reads free memory: vLLM refuses to start when free memory is under utilization x total, and another program holds the rest. It reads the GPU now: run it with nothing else on the GPU for the share the model will have. A share below what the weights need (plus 2 GiB for activations) is never set: vLLM's default stands, and it names the shortfall itself at start.{vllm.gpu_warning}
knobs.reason_default: vLLM's default: {gpu_free_gib:.1f} of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB is free; a lower share is derived only when the free memory is under 0.92 of the total and still holds the weights plus 2 GiB for activations.{vllm.gpu_warning}
knobs.reason_missing: vLLM's default: the GPU's memory could not be read here, so the share is not checked against what is free
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/cache.py:103 (default 0.92); vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:543-555 (free < utilization x total refuses to start); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1326

knobs.name: --kv-cache-dtype
knobs.controls: the KV cache's element type (auto: the model's, bf16 here)
knobs.formula: 'fp8' if model_weight_bytes + kv_bytes_per_token * context_tokens > vllm.gpu_share * gpu_total_bytes else None
knobs.reason: fp8: the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and a {context_tokens}-token bf16 KV cache ({kv_bytes_per_token:,.0f} bytes per token) do not fit vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB; fp8 halves the cache. Quality is not measured here
knobs.reason_missing: auto (vLLM's): the GPU's memory could not be read here, so the fit of a {context_tokens}-token cache is not checked
knobs.reason_default: auto: the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and a {context_tokens}-token cache at the model's type fit vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB (activations and graphs not counted)
knobs.not_applicable: the model has no per-token KV cache
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/cache.py:39-58 (CacheDType), :123 (default auto); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1334; the same fit as workflow/recommend.context_figures

knobs.name: --cpu-offload-gb
knobs.controls: GiB of weights per GPU kept in pinned host memory and read by the GPU over the link (UVA zero-copy) in each forward
knobs.formula: min(gib_ceil(model_weight_bytes + vllm.kv_bytes_per_token * context_tokens - vllm.gpu_share * gpu_total_bytes), gib_floor(usable_ram_bytes) - vllm.process_headroom_gib)
knobs.reason: what the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and the {context_tokens}-token KV cache need beyond vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB: a lower bound (activations and graphs not counted). The offloaded weights live in pinned host RAM, so it is capped at the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable less {vllm.process_headroom_gib} GiB kept free for the vLLM process itself (a margin, not a measurement). A model that does not fit the GPU share plus that RAM is refused before this row
knobs.not_applicable: the weights and the {context_tokens}-token KV cache fit the GPU: nothing to offload
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/offload.py:23-32 (cpu_offload_gb, UVA); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1402

knobs.name: --cpu-offload-params
knobs.controls: which parameters (name segments) the offload takes first; unset: any, in load order, up to --cpu-offload-gb
knobs.reason: experts: a decode step reads only the routed experts of each layer, while it reads every dense weight, so offloading experts moves the least-read bytes over the link when writing replies. A long prompt touches nearly every expert, so prompts read the offloaded bytes in full either way
knobs.reason_default: unset: a dense model reads every weight each forward, so no subset is cheaper to keep in host memory
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/offload.py:34-44 (segment match, 'mlp.experts.w2_weight' matches 'experts'); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1404

knobs.name: --offload-backend
knobs.controls: how offloaded weights reach the GPU: uva (zero-copy reads of pinned host memory) or prefetch (whole layers in groups, copied ahead asynchronously, --offload-group-size)
knobs.reason: auto selects uva when only --cpu-offload-gb is set; prefetch is the other backend, set by layer groups instead of GiB. The two are not measured against each other here, so vLLM's pick stands
knobs.evidence: vllm/model_executor/offloader/base.py:156-162 (auto: prefetch if offload_group_size > 0, uva if cpu_offload_gb > 0); vllm/config/offload.py:47-75 (prefetch), :83; vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1400

knobs.name: --max-num-batched-tokens
